standard_prerequisites.name: Comparability graph of a partially ordered set
standard_prerequisites.statement: Given a partially ordered set, its comparability graph has the elements as vertices and an undirected edge between two vertices exactly when the corresponding elements are comparable; the article's own description is retained at source lines 117-120.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the class of graphs into which the lower-bound argument must fail to split the edge set, and into which the upper-bound argument explicitly splits it.

standard_prerequisites.name: The partition number p(G) and the cover number c(G)
standard_prerequisites.statement: p(G) is the minimum m such that the edge set of G is the union of m edge-disjoint comparability subgraphs of G, and c(G) is the same number without the edge-disjointness requirement, so that c(G) is at most p(G); retained at source lines 128-129.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proposition asserts p(H) = c(H) = 3, so both parameters must be fixed before the statement can be read; the article notes at source line 130 that p(H) >= c(H) holds always.

standard_prerequisites.name: The graph H_{9,4}
standard_prerequisites.statement: H_{9,4} has 72 vertices and is obtained from the cartesian product K_9 square K_4, that is the line graph of the complete bipartite graph K_{9,4}, by attaching one pendant edge at every vertex; the article's own construction is retained at source lines 631-632.
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the graph of the counted proposition with the vertex set K union W, the nine columns and four rows of K and the pendant neighbours, which the proof enumerates.

core_obligations: Write the vertex set of H as the disjoint union of K = {v_{i,j}} and W = {w_{i,j}} and name the j-th row X_j = {v_{i,j} : i} and the i-th column Y_i = {v_{i,j} : j} (source lines 646-649).

Record the three kinds of edges of H: the pendant edges e_{i,j} = {v_{i,j}, w_{i,j}}, the complete graphs induced on each row X_j and the complete graphs induced on each column Y_i (source lines 651-654).

Prove that H is perfect: the cartesian product K_9 square K_4 is the line graph of the complete bipartite graph K_{9,4} and is therefore perfect, and attaching pendant edges preserves perfectness (source lines 656-657).

Prove the upper bound c(H) <= p(H) <= 3 by taking the transitive orientations of the complete graphs on the rows, those of the complete graphs on the columns, and any orientation of the pendant edges, and checking that these three comparability subgraphs partition the edge set of H (source lines 659-661).
Assume for a contradiction that H is the union of two comparability subgraphs A and B and fix transitive orientations of both (source lines 663-667).

Define a vertex v_{i,j} to be A-good or B-good when it is the midpoint of an oriented two-edge path inside its row with both edges in A respectively in B, and good when it is good for at least one of the two subgraphs; derive that a bad vertex must be maximal or minimal in both restricted orientations, hence has one of four types (source lines 669-678).

Show that within a single row two bad vertices of the same type cannot be joined by an edge inside the subgraph that realises that type, so every row contains at most four bad vertices and therefore at least five good ones; hence K contains at least twenty good vertices and some column contains at least three of them (source lines 680-688).

Finish the contradiction on three good vertices of one column: two of them cannot be good for different subgraphs, so all three are good for the same one, whence all three connecting edges must lie in the other subgraph and form an oriented path there; taking the middle vertex of that path and the pendant edge at it yields an edge that transitivity forces but that H does not contain (source lines 690-700).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the vertex set K union W, the rows X_j and the columns Y_i, and list the three edge types of H.
Show that H is perfect, as the line graph of K_{9,4} with pendant edges attached.
Build three comparability subgraphs from the rows, the columns and the pendant edges to get p(H) <= 3.
Assume a two-colouring by comparability subgraphs A and B, orient both transitively, and classify vertices as good or bad with four bad types.
Bound the bad vertices per row by four, obtain twenty good vertices in K and three good vertices in one column.
Derive the final contradiction from three equally good vertices of a column together with the pendant edge at the middle of the induced oriented path.
Conclude that two comparability subgraphs do not suffice.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Proposition H9（源 637-638 行，证明 642-701 行，共 60 行）：证明 72 个顶点的图 H_{9,4} 是完美图且 p(H)=c(H)=3。关键操作不是例行核验：上界要看出把行完全图、列完全图与任意定向的悬挂边分别作传递定向恰好给出三个可比子图（659-661 行）；下界要假设存在两个可比子图 A、B 并各自传递定向，再引入「好点/坏点」与坏点的四种类型，用「同行同类型的两个坏点不能在对应子图内相邻」证明每行至多四个坏点、于是 K 中至少二十个好点、某列至少三个好点（669-688 行），最后在这三个好点上用传递性导出图 H 中并不存在的边（690-700 行）。难点在于好点/坏点的分类与「同列三个好点必属同一子图」的论证是作者为这个小图专门设计的组合论证，任何一步的类型计数都必须精确；原文位置在证明的 675-688 行与 690-700 行。
